articles.title: ‘A bolt from the blue’: Shock cancer diagnosis raises uncertainty for Leo’s papacy
articles.summary: Thousands of people congregated in the Vatican’s St. Peter’s Square on Wednesday for a Mass that Pope Leo should have been presiding over. Instead, another senior Catholic Church official took his place, while the first American pope recovered in a hospital after being diagnosed with lung cancer following an operation to remove a lobe of his right lung.
articles.body: Thousands of people congregated in the Vatican’s St. Peter’s Square on Wednesday for a Mass that Pope Leo should have been presiding over. Instead, another senior Catholic Church official took his place, while the first American pope recovered in a hospital after being diagnosed with lung cancer following an operation to remove a lobe of his right lung. The pope’s cancer diagnosis, confirmed on Tuesday, has caused alarm across the Catholic world. Pope Leo was elected less than 18 months ago at the age of 69, the youngest man chosen to lead the Catholic Church since Pope John Paul II almost 40 years earlier. Given his relatively youthful age, the view in the Vatican and among church leaders was that Leo had a long papacy in front of him. That assumption is now being tested. The era of papal health struggles had, many in the Vatican hoped, been put aside in the short term. Leo’s predecessor Pope Francis, elected at 76 and with part of his right lung missing, had a series of health problems towards the end of his pontificate, and spent weeks in the Gemelli hospital with pneumonia. Francis, who had served as pope since 2013, died of a stroke and heart failure in April 2025. Pope Leo’s approach to his health has been steady, sensible and balanced. He goes to the papal retreat at Castel Gandolfo outside of Rome every Tuesday for a day off. He plays tennis, he swims, and as a cardinal had a personal trainer. All of that added to the shock of his hospital admission. “No one expected it,” Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Holy See Secretary of State, told reporters, likening it to a “bolt from the blue.” The cardinal, speaking before the cancer diagnosis was confirmed, added: “I am worried.” Leo XIV has cancelled all his audiences until October 20 as he continues his recovery. The doctors are confident that the cancer was removed during surgery, but further tests are needed. For the pope, near term plans are up in the air. Leo went into hospital in the middle of a major Vatican gathering of bishops and church leaders, which he had convened. The discussions focused on how the church can support couples and families a decade on from a major document issued by Pope Francis, which opened the possibility of divorced and remarried Catholics being able to receive communion. The meeting was an example of Leo, in his own style, seeking to implement the reforms begun by his predecessor. But his operation meant he could not take part in the Mass that concluded the gathering or take an active part in the meetings. “It’s very concerning and I think the more recent news that it is actually a cancer is very worrying for everybody,” Archbishop Tim Costelloe, the president of the Australian Bishops’ Conference, said just off St Peter’s Square following the Mass on Wednesday. The archbishop had been taking part in the gathering and said he’d written to the pope on behalf of his country’s bishops assuring him of prayers and support. Questions are being asked of future papal travel. From Nov. 6-17, the pope is due to be in Latin America for an intense three country tour to Uruguay, Argentina and an emotional “homecoming” to Peru, where he served as a missionary and bishop. His packed itinerary includes 14 flights, 50 events and visits to some high-altitude parts of the continent. Archbishop Costelloe says the latest developments “inevitably” raise questions about the forthcoming trip, but stressed Leo is “a strong man, he’s a fit man” and there was plenty of hope he “can get past this.” As of Wednesday, no changes have been announced to the dates of the trip. Leo XIV, a meticulous and details-oriented leader, made sure everything was in order before his operation. A couple of days before announcing he was going in for surgery, the pope confirmed the election of Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, a high-ranking Vatican official from the Philippines, to the important role of Dean of the College of Cardinals. This is the position held by the fictional Cardinal Lawrence played by Ralph Fiennes in the movie “Conclave,” released in the months before the real-life papal election that chose Leo. The appointment of Tagle, who stood in for Leo to preside at Wednesday’s mass at the Vatican, has acquired a new significance with the pope in the hospital. The dean, who is the “first among equals” leader of the college, plays a crucial role in presiding over a conclave (providing he’s under 80) and the pre-conclave meetings. Any future papal election is considered far into the future. But the appointment of the 69-year-old Tagle, a charismatic figure previously tipped as a possible pope, was an important piece of housekeeping. Leo’s cancer diagnosis has been met by an outpouring of public support. It offers an opportunity for him to connect with so many other individuals and families who have been affected by the illness. “Pope Leo has shown compassionate solidarity with so many people encountering struggles and challenges in their lives,” Fr. Joseph Farrell, the leader of the Augustinian religious order and a friend of the pope, told CNN. “As Augustinians, we invite all people to show that same loving, prayerful solidarity with the Holy Father.” Leo is an Augustinian and a former leader of the order. There is a history of cancer in the pope’s family, with his eldest brother Louis Prevost currently being treated for the illness, which he was first diagnosed with in 2017. The pope’s mother, Mildred, died of cancer in 1990. His father, also Louis, died of colon cancer and heart disease in 1997. While inside the Vatican there is worry about his health, the cogs of the church’s central administration will keep on turning. “It’s not a case of running around pulling hair out,” one official told CNN. “We are getting on with the work inside the dicasteries (Vatican departments) which support the pope’s ministry.” And the pope can still govern the church from his hospital bed. Those who know the pope well say he will be keen to bounce back. Elise Allen, who interviewed the pope in July 2025 for her book on Leo XIV, described the situation as a “waiting game” but it was important not to jump to too many conclusions. “He’s a very hard worker, he’s very determined, he’s going to want to get back into the swing of things very quickly if that’s possible,” she told CNN. Allen said, however, that his hospitalization may lead him to “scale back” some of his appointments and commitments. She also pointed out that his last major health crisis, as a young missionary sent to Peru, was definitive. In 1985, soon after arriving in the country, Leo was struck down with Typhoid fever. Allen said that it was a turning point as, following his recovery, it led him to embrace his work in South America. Both popes John Paul II and Francis show how the role of pontiff involves an element of public suffering. And as recent conclaves have elected men in their late 60s and 70s, health difficulties are never far around the corner. “Fragility deserves special attention,” Leo XIV said in his speech to the family life gathering last week. “The experience of families has something to teach everyone, since fragility belongs to our common human condition and therefore also to the life of the Church.” The pope is now embracing that same fragility and uncertainty that many others with a similar diagnosis have faced.

articles.title: In 2014, a couple bought an 18th-century Scottish church and renovated it into a five-bedroom home and working bistro; the 4,779-square-foot property is now on the market with offers over £550,000
articles.summary: The Old Kirk has been a church, then a bistro, and now, if the sellers get their way, it could become a family home.
articles.body: The Old Kirk has been a church, then a bistro, and now, if the sellers get their way, it could become a family home. The property sits in the village of Fordyce, a few miles from Banff in north-east Scotland. The five-bedroom detached house is now up for sale with offers over £550,000.Old-world charm and modern roomsIn the 1700s, this building was a place of worship. Much of its original character has survived. Chris and Alison Temple bought the church in 2014 and undertook an extensive renovation to turn it into a home with a business attached. Savills, the estate agency that listed the property, dates the conversion to around the same time, which fits the couple’s timeline.The property extends to around 4,779 sq. ft. across two floors. While converting the church into a home and a business, the couple made sure they preserved what they could. According to the listing, they carefully preserved many features of the original building, including the beautiful arched windows and soaring ceiling. These allow natural light to flood indoors. But they also ensured the property had modern elements. “The conversion also embraces a strong contemporary design, creating a hugely impressive and substantial home,” the listing says. The stone building still retains the shape of a church, with tall windows and high walls that give it presence from the outside.The Old Kirk opens through double doors with an attractive fanlight into a tiled entrance hall, which leads to a large reception room ideal for dining. The open-plan kitchen and living area, with a double-height ceiling and a mezzanine gallery with glass balustrades above, is another highlight of the home. Engineered oak flooring and underfloor heating run throughout the house. The bespoke sliding barn-style doors combine traditional character with a modern touch. A gallery sits above the kitchen, and that is where the lounge is located. The couple also upgraded the kitchen with professional-standard Siemens appliances, a stainless-steel island and a commercial-sized fridge.The home has five bedrooms, two of which are at the rear of the ground floor, each with its own shower room. Upstairs, an oak staircase leads to a large living and dining room. It has a high ceiling, a glazed balcony overlooking the kitchen and a double log stove. There is room for three large sofas and a big dining table. The remaining three bedrooms each have their own character. One has bookshelves with a library ladder, while the main suite has both a shower and a bath.The bistroThe large tiled reception hall, reached through double doors, now serves as the bistro. It has individual tables and chairs, including green leather banquettes. This space could be anything the new buyer wants it to be. Until a buyer is found, the Old Kirk Bistro continues to serve lunches and evening meals. For now, the family home and the restaurant share the same roof.The house is surrounded by stone walls, flowerbeds and mature trees. “Occupying a peaceful and highly attractive setting, The Old Kirk enjoys beautifully landscaped grounds extending to approximately 0.35 acres,” the listing says. A stream runs through the nearby village. The garden provides “a wonderful sense of shelter and privacy”, according to the listing. Savills describes the setting as giving the property “a rare sense of tranquillity and timeless charm”. It is hard to argue with that when you picture the garden in summer! The property is on the market with offers over £550,000.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Mexico to force Meta, TikTok, and X to better protect minors on platform
articles.summary: Mexico will require the digital platforms to protect minors from violent and sexual content.
articles.body:
Mexican ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠President Claudia ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sheinbaum signed a presidential decree requiring digital platforms, including TikTok, Meta and X, to protect children from violent, sexual and other harmful content online.

The decree establishes that digital platforms must, by design, restrict exposure to content involving violence, harassment or sexual abuse, as well as immediately remove any risky material from the profiles of minors.

Sheinbaum said on Wednesday that the government would back legislation to penalise companies that fail to implement the decree.

“If no progress is made, it would become a law,” she told a news conference on Tuesday.

“The goal is for digital platforms to take on some of the responsibility and refrain from disseminating, promoting, or spreading content related to this type of information — including criminal acts or violent behaviour,” Sheinbaum had said earlier when she indicated she would introduce the decree.

The decree comes after an attack by two 18-year-olds on their former high school in the northern ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌state of Coahuila in early October that killed one and wounded three others.

Digital platforms will have one month to comply with the decree, government adviser Luisa Maria Alcalde said.

Officials said they had already discussed the matter with representatives of social media outlets and streaming platforms such as Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei.

Last August, Meta, for example, agreed to pay an $ 18bn settlement in a major US federal case accusing it of endangering children, and was forced to introduce new safety features to platforms including Instagram and Facebook. The lawsuit alleged Meta had violated the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act by collecting, ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠retaining, and using personal data from children under 13 without proper parental consent.

Mexico’s move follows a broader global push to protect minors online, with governments in Europe and Australia tightening oversight of digital platforms and US states pursuing a range of child-safety measures.

Brazil has also moved to strengthen protections for children online. Such measures have raised questions over how to protect minors while safeguarding privacy and freedom of expression.

articles.title: Albania protests: Student protesters attack government ministries in Tirana
articles.summary: Thousands of students in Albania are calling for better university conditions and job prospects, but buildings have been set on fire in the unrest.
articles.body:
Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.

The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects.

Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked.

Albania's Deputy Prime Minister ​Albana Koçiu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".

Riot police have clashed with the protesters, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse them.

One demonstrator, Enida Bimi, told Reuters news agency that the protest is not just for the students, but "for all the people of Albania".

"The people are very angry at the system. They need to change everything. With this corruption all around, the crime and everything else is happening. And the people now are angry. They need to change the system," Bimi said.

Another protester, Arber Leshi, said people are angry at "the most corrupt government our country has ever seen".

Education Mirela Kumbaro said that while she respects the right to protest, "civic student protest and violence against public buildings and property are two different things".

Officials have criticised the behaviour of some protesters.

"Setting fire to an institution is not a peaceful protest. It is an act that endanger's peoples lives", said economy minister Delina Ibrahimaj, responding to a video appearing to show protesters throwing rocks at the finance ministry building.

Sixteen people were arrested "in connection with violent acts" during Tuesday's protest, Albania's state-run news agency said.

Sali Berisha, the leader of the opposition - the Democratic Party of Albania - has praised the protesters.

"The streets and squares of Tirana have never seen lions like these students," he said during an evening meeting on Wednesday, Albania's state-run news agency Ata reported.

This student-led protest comes after months of anti-government protests, known as the Flamingo Revolution , which is calling for Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

The protests were sparked by a luxury tourism project linked to Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner , which fuelled anger over alleged corruption and a lack of transparency from Rama's government.

articles.title: Christian teacher was 'quite shocked' after getting fired for telling student she's pro-life
articles.summary: Anita Meston says she was fired from a United Kingdom school after telling a student she was pro-life, and her case now heads to an employment tribunal.
articles.body: A Christian teacher in the United Kingdom says she was fired after telling a student she was pro-life during a classroom discussion, describing her shock at losing her job over remarks she says were simply an honest response to a student's question. Anita Meston, a secondary school teacher who taught French and humanities at Biddick Academy, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview she was covering a history lesson about the bombing of Dresden when students began asking about her views on Israel and abortion. Meston said she initially asked students to compare the bombing of Dresden with the conflict between Israel and Gaza in an effort to encourage classroom discussion. FIRED SCHOOL COUNSELOR LOSES AGAIN AFTER FREE SPEECH FIGHT OVER GENDER-THEMED BOOKS IN HIS OFFICE As the discussion progressed, a student asked whether she supported abortion. "And I said, 'No, I'm pro-life,'" Meston recalled. "And she said, ‘Well, what does that mean?’" Meston said she explained that her Christian beliefs would prevent her from participating in an abortion if she worked in a medical setting. "And I said, also, I know women who've had abortions who've regretted them," Meston said. "And she then responded with, ‘Well I know women who've had abortions who haven't regretted them,’ and I said, ‘Well that's fair enough.’ And then we moved back to the lesson, whatever was left of it." NASHVILLE SCHOOL PULLS LGBT BOOKS AFTER CHRISTIAN TEACHER WAS DISCIPLINED FOR REFUSING TO READ ONE But Meston claims the exchange cost her her job. "I was quite shocked actually," she told Fox News Digital, describing a subsequent meeting with the school's head teacher. Meston said the head teacher accused her of sharing personal opinions in class before informing her that the school could no longer employ her. "She said, 'Thank you very much for your service, but we can't keep you on at the school,'" Meston recalled. The teacher said the experience left her feeling humiliated despite believing she had done nothing wrong. "Well, it's shock, isn't it?" Meston said. "And then, also feeling … humiliated in a way. Although I knew that I hadn't really done anything wrong, you still get that sense that, you know, you're being kicked out of your job and having to tell other teachers why and the first teacher I spoke to actually said to me, ‘Well, a lot of us have similar views to you, but we're not keen. ... We're frightened to express them.’" TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS Jeremiah Igunnubole, Meston's attorney, told Fox News Digital he believes the dismissal was connected to her expression of Christian beliefs and violated protections afforded under British law. "Well, teachers should teach children how to think, not what to think," Igunnubole said. CHRISTIAN WOMAN PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO NEW 'ORWELLIAN' CHARGES FOR STANDING AND SILENT PRAYER He argued that Meston had not attempted to impose her views on students but had merely responded to a question before returning to the lesson. "She did not seek to indoctrinate. She did not seek to impose her beliefs on the students. She simply answered a question," he said. WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR 5TH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION Igunnubole said Meston's case is proceeding before the Newcastle Employment Tribunal, where a preliminary hearing is scheduled to address the basic arguments and establish a timetable for future proceedings. A spokesperson for The North East Learning Trust, which Biddick Academy is a part of, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "While we are not able to comment on this individual case, we have a clear staff code of conduct, which is consistently applied to protect the safety and wellbeing of our children at all times." articles.title: 'See a true Holocaust': Religion professor indicted after anonymous antisemitic posts exposed
articles.summary: Guangtian Ha, a Haverford College religion professor, faces a federal indictment over alleged antisemitic cyberstalking of a Jewish colleague.
articles.body: An associate professor at Haverford College is facing a federal cyberstalking charge after an alleged months-long online antisemitic intimidation campaign against a Jewish colleague and his family. Messages that prosecutors say the professor sent include antisemitic language and threats. Guangtian Ha, an associate professor of religion at Haverford College, was arrested Oct. 6. The indictment lays out a series of serious allegations. According to a federal indictment, Ha carried out the alleged intimidation campaign from Oct. 9, 2025, through May 20, 2026, using anonymous X accounts to send threatening messages and share images of his Jewish colleague's mailbox. Lori Lowenthal Marcus, who serves as the legal director of The Deborah Project, a legal group that previously filed a Title VI civil rights lawsuit against Haverford on behalf of Jewish students, told Fox News Digital the messages reveal a harsh truth about anti-Zionism on campus. "Everything that I had heard from Guangtian Ha, the accused here, had been directed at Zionists," Lowenthal Marcus said. "What he revealed in his anonymous posts to another faculty member was 95% about hatred of Jews and death threats towards Jews and disgusting language towards Jews." JEWISH CAMPUS LIFE AT A ‘CROSSING POINT’ AS STUDENTS WEIGH ANTISEMITISM RISKS, NEW REPORT SHOWS Lowenthal Marcus said the messages exemplify a concern that Jews at Haverford had raised, that the word "Zionist" was being used as "a code word for Jews." On Oct. 9, 2025, Ha allegedly used the X account "America1st33509" when replying to the victim's X posts with an image of the victim's own home mailbox and the eyes emoji, according to the indictment. Then, in the winter of 2026 — the indictment states that this occurred "in or about January 2026, through in or about February 2026" — Ha allegedly used the account "America1stLM" to post several "threatening and harassing messages." "LM" in Ha's username likely refers to Lower Merion Township, a Jewish area in Pennsylvania near Haverford College's campus. Using the "America1stLM" handle, Ha allegedly sent the victim messages such as "Jew, get the f--- out of my country," "Jew pig, get the f--- out of lower Merion," "If jews are so special then. they should also be placed in special camps and receive special treatments," and "LM jews are going to have it big time, jew. Remember this. You scums have had it too easy. Goyim are taking America back, blood-guzzling demons." JEWISH STUDENT SUES NEW YORK SCHOOL ON OCT 7 ANNIVERSARY OVER 'RELENTLESS ANTISEMITIC HARASSMENT' The indictment states that the victim and his family "enacted security precautions" in response to those messages. However, this did not stop Ha's alleged harassment. Prosecutors allege that Ha continued the harassment, mocking those security measures in a Feb. 27, 2026, post that read: "@[Victim 1] The goyim have woken up, jew. Run. Flee. Leave. Blurring your home on google map and installing a security camera next to your mailbox won't help." Months later, on April 15, 2026, Ha, using the handle "Im_GoyimDL" demanded in a post that the victim, whom he referred to as a "fat jew," leave Lower Merion Township. Approximately one minute after that post, according to the indictment, Ha wrote "@[Victim 1] Jew, watch your [Victim 1's minor son's true name.] There shall be a sign." According to the indictment, Ha sent additional messages in April 2026 and May 2026, including posts that contained the victim's home address. The indictment also describes messages from that period that included a pro-Nazi sign-off and a threat invoking the Holocaust. In April 2026, Ha allegedly tagged the victim and wrote, "Nothing wrong to hate jews. We started to decline the moment we stopped hating, eradicating and expelling jews. Babylonians knew, the Romans knew, the Spaniards knew. American jews have been exposed. F--- anti-Zionism. HH." The indictment notes that "HH" is a common abbreviation for "Heil Hitler." The next month, Ha posted, "@[Victim 1] Eliminate the jewish cockroaches. Exterminate the jewish state. [Victim 1], you will have nowhere to go. Your family has no future in the US. Give it another 10 years, and you shall see a true holocaust." DOJ SUES UCLA OVER ALLEGED ‘JUDENREIN’ CONDITIONS DURING ANTI-ISRAEL ENCAMPMENT The threats from Ha became so serious that the FBI got involved with the case. When reached for comment, the bureau referred Fox News Digital to court documents. Ha, according to the indictment, "frequently utilized virtual private networks to obfuscate his internet protocol address and make tracing of the source of the messages more difficult." A virtual private network, often referred to as a VPN, can help hide one's internet protocol (IP) address, obscuring a user's location. Despite the attempts to disguise his identity, federal authorities were able to trace the messages back to Ha. Ha was ordered detained in federal custody pending trial following a hearing Tuesday, according to an Oct. 13 announcement from the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Haverford College declined to give further comment on the situation. However, the college's president released a statement on the day of Ha's arrest. "I am deeply distressed by these allegations and want to state in the plainest of terms that any form of harassment or discrimination based on identity is unacceptable, antithetical to our values and has no place at Haverford," Haverford College President Wendy Raymond's statement read. "Professor Ha, who was on sabbatical leave and not teaching this academic year, has been placed on administrative leave and barred from campus while the criminal process moves forward." In the statement, Raymond confirmed that a representative of Haverford College has been in contact with Ha's alleged victims. She also thanked the FBI, Campus Safety and Haverford Township Police Department. "I am heartbroken and furious at the possibility that an individual within our community would seek to inflict such pain on another," Raymond wrote. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Lowenthal Marcus noted that while political speech about the Middle East is protected under academic freedom, harassment and threats cross a clear legal line. "For some reason, everyone has been screaming about academic freedom and free speech rights and became free speech absolutists when it came to protecting the Jews. And that's got to end," Lowenthal Marcus told Fox News Digital. While the federal indictment focuses on anonymous threats, Ha's social media posts were already at the center of a federal civil rights lawsuit filed against the college. The Deborah Project cited several of Ha's posts in a 2024 lawsuit against Haverford on behalf of Jewish students. In one post, Ha appeared to threaten people in his "little world," which the lawsuit contends refers to Haverford, who were silent about the situation in Gaza. "I will forever remember who in my little world are silent on this genocide or even tacitly support it, with whatever excuse they have managed to convince themselves of, and I will never forgive them. I know their names and I know their faces. Never forgive. No reconciliation," Ha wrote. In another one of the public posts, Ha, an associate professor of religion, wrote, "Zionism is fundamentally a modern racist ideology that has next to nothing to do with Judaism as an ancient religion." "He deserves no credibility, but, of course, students and others who read from a professor of religion making a statement like that, they are going to give him," Lowenthal Marcus said of Ha's statement in which he attempted to sever Zionism from Judaism. Lowenthal Marcus expressed hope that the indictment of Ha would force not just Haverford College, but educational institutions nationwide to recognize the dangerous reality of online antisemitic harassment. "I hope this will be a deterrent to others who would act as he has acted, and will also be an impetus for investigators, for educational institutions and other kinds of institutions to recognize the code word 'Zionist' for what it is," she told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital reached out to Haverford Township Police Department for comment but did not receive an immediate response. No legal representatives for Ha have been named publicly.

articles.title: World’s oldest shipwreck found off coast of Turkiye
articles.summary: Clay analysis traces recovered storage jars to early history workshops operating across the Jordan Valley.
articles.body:
Turkiye’s Culture Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy has said the country unearthed ancient treasures from what he called “the world’s oldest shipwreck”.

Underwater excavations near Kekova Island in the southern Antalya province uncovered ceramic storage jars dating back 4,700 years to the Early Bronze Age, Ersoy announced in a post on X on Wednesday.

While the vessel’s wooden hull did not survive, archaeologists recovered the ancient storage jars following an underwater excavation project launched earlier this year.

The jars, believed to have transported olive oil or wine, provide concrete evidence of early maritime trade and cultural exchange across the eastern Mediterranean, according to the ministry.

Clay analysis indicated the containers were manufactured in workshops in the Jordan Valley, matching similar styles previously found in Egypt, Turkiye, and Greece that illustrate extensive Bronze Age sea routes.

One vessel was singled out for its unique design, featuring nine markings and two holes in its body that suggest it may have been used to churn butter or cheese.

Researchers believe the ship was sailing from the Levantine coast towards modern-day Hisarlik in Turkiye or the island of Crete in Greece when it capsized and sank.

The excavation was directed by Hakan Oniz, an associate professor of archaeology at Akdeniz University.

Speaking to the BBC, the professor said when his team first found the wreck four years ago, the jars only appeared to be a century or two old.

“However, we later became excited when we saw the same amphora forms in a publication on Egyptian archaeology and returned to the site,” he said. “Indeed, they were similar to those found at the Giza pyramids in Egypt. We were incredibly excited.”

The discovery has “shed light on the deep-rooted history of maritime trade along the Anatolian coasts,” added Ersoy.

articles.title: Families of Trinidadian men killed in US boat strike demand accountability
articles.summary: The Trump administration has killed at least 239 people in boat strikes denounced as extrajudicial killings.
articles.body:
The families of two missing men from the Caribbean country of Trinidad and Tobago have marked the one-year anniversary of their disappearance by calling for accountability from the United States.

Since September last year, the US military has undertaken a campaign of attacking small boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean, on the basis that they were transporting “narco-terrorists”.

But critics have called the boat strikes an illegal campaign of extrajudicial killings .

On Wednesday, the families of Chad Joseph and Rishi Samaroo issued a statement remembering the two men, who they said were killed in one of the US boat strikes on October 14, 2025.

The families are currently pursuing a wrongful death lawsuit in the state of Massachusetts, supported by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU). They have argued that Joseph and Samaroo were fishermen and farm workers, not drug-traffickers.

“The last year has been devastating without Chad in our lives. Chad was the heart of our family. He was loving, generous and caring and always there for us. We all miss him terribly,” said Joseph’s mother, Lenore Burnley.

“A year later, we are still grieving and seeking justice for his death. We will always mourn losing Chad but hope that this lawsuit will be a step towards justice for him and the family.”

Four other people were killed in the attack on October 14, 2025, when a missile struck a vessel returning to Trinidad and Tobago from nearby Venezuela.

The families have said Samaroo and Joseph had been working in Venezuela to support their families.

Both men called their families two days before embarking on the trip home to the islands. They were never heard from again.

The boat strike campaign, launched under US President Donald Trump, has killed at least 239 people since September 2025.

But the US government has provided little evidence to prove its claims that those on board were trafficking drugs. It has also not publicly identified the victims.

In several cases — from Colombia to Ecuador to Trinidad and Tobago — relatives have stepped forward to say that their loved ones were among those killed, and that they were fishermen with no connection to the drug trade.

Separately, the family of Colombian fisherman Alejandro Carranza has filed a complaint with the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, accusing the Trump administration of violating his right to life when it allegedly bombed his boat on September 15, 2025.

Samaroo and Joseph’s lawsuit was filed in January and is being heard by a US federal court in the city of Boston, Massachusetts.

“Not a day goes by when our family doesn’t think about our brother Rishi,” said Sallycar Korasingh, Samaroo’s youngest sister.

“Rishi was a good person, loved by his family and community. The last year without him in our lives has been heartbreaking. My brother and family deserve justice. We will continue fighting for answers and the accountability we deserve.”

Legal scholars have noted that, even if those killed were involved in criminal activity, the strikes would still amount to extrajudicial killings.

Under international law, it is generally illegal to use military force for civilian law enforcement. Drug trafficking is not considered an act of war, but rather a civilian crime.

“For a year now, our clients have had to live without their loved ones and without justice in the name of President Trump’s lawless killing campaign,” said Jeff Stein, staff attorney with ACLU’s National Security Project.

The group is representing the families in their lawsuit, along with the Center for Constitutional Rights.

“These illegal strikes at sea have devastated countless families, terrified communities, and made us all less safe,” Stein said. “We won’t stop fighting for accountability. We urge leaders in both Congress and the executive branch to finally end this illegal campaign before anyone else is killed.”

articles.title: Woman found floating in sea after going overboard from Royal Caribbean ship
articles.summary: A 44-year-old woman clung to a lifebuoy for 20 hours in the Ionian Sea after reportedly jumping from Royal Caribbean's Odyssey of the Seas near Zakynthos.
articles.body: A woman who went overboard from a Royal Caribbean cruise ship was rescued after spending 20 hours in the water clinging to a lifebuoy, the Hellenic Coast Guard said. The 44-year-old Salvadoran national was traveling aboard Odyssey of the Seas as it sailed through the Ionian Sea near the island of Zakynthos on Saturday, the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs told USA Today. The cargo ship MSC Rossella III was assisting in the search and spotted the woman inside the bright orange lifebuoy in dark waters. The vessel alerted authorities, and a Greek Coast Guard crew arrived to toss her ropes and pull her to safety. CRUISE PASSENGER JUMPS FROM BALCONY AND DIES AFTER FALLING OVERBOARD INTO OCEAN The woman reportedly told authorities she jumped off the ship because she "wanted to disembark," a Coast Guard spokesperson told Agence France-Presse, adding that "she was 20 hours at sea." Following her rescue, she was transported to the port of Katakolo and brought to a local hospital, where a prosecutor ordered a psychiatric evaluation, according to the Hellenic Coast Guard. CARNIVAL CRUISE SHIP PASSENGER DIES AFTER FALLING FROM BALCONY – FBI INVESTIGATES HIGH-SEAS HORROR Fox News Digital reached out to Royal Caribbean for comment. The incident follows a similar stunt last year when a man jumped off Royal Caribbean's Rhapsody of the Seas in San Juan, Puerto Rico, in an attempt to evade nearly $17,000 in gambling debt. articles.title: Furious crowds protest sky-high housing costs and mass tourism in major city
articles.summary: Barcelona's mayor says tourist taxes still aren't high enough as Spain's mass tourism and vacation rental crisis continue to spark angry and loud protests by residents.
articles.body: Growing tensions between tourists and locals hit a boiling point in Spain recently as hundreds of thousands of residents flooded the streets of Barcelona, Madrid and other Spanish cities to protest skyrocketing housing costs. A housing affordability crisis is at the center of the unrest, fueled in part by short-term vacation rentals, an issue Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni has publicly addressed. Residents are arguing mass tourism has priced them out, with real estate companies converting apartments into lucrative vacation stays. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez addressed the issue recently at an event in Barcelona. ANGRY LOCALS BLOCK FAMOUS BEACH AS MASS TOURISM PROTESTS ESCALATE AT VACATION HOT SPOT "Finding an apartment in Barcelona definitely gave me a better understanding of how competitive the housing market can be," travel writer Jordi Lippe-McGraw, who moved to Barcelona from New York City six weeks ago, told Fox News Digital. "It's a city where so many people want to live. There's a lot of pressure on available housing." Barcelona and the surrounding region welcomed a total of 26.1 million visitors in 2025, which generated an estimated $15.4 billion in direct tourism spending, according to the Barcelona Tourism Observatory. Frustrated locals have protested loudly and defiantly. BRAZEN PICKPOCKETS PREY ON VULNERABLE TOURISTS AS VACATION ISLAND IS SWARMED BY MILLIONS Amid the pressure, the federal and local governments are trying to implement change. "Barcelona began rethinking tourism ... back in 2017," José Antonio Donaire, the commissioner for sustainable tourism, told The New York Times this summer. "But the message of the city now is: Not one tourist more." In September, the forced eviction of María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old Spanish pensioner, became a symbol of the affordability crisis, Fox News Digital reported earlier. After she died Oct. 7, thousands took to the streets in Madrid, Valencia, Barcelona, Hospitalet de Llobregat, Málaga and other cities. AMERICANS EMERGE AS SOUGHT-AFTER VISITORS AS VACATION ISLAND FACES TOURISM BACKLASH Short-term vacation rentals are part of the dispute. On April 1, Barcelona combined a flat $5.60 (€5.00) city surcharge with the regional Catalan tourist tax, creating one of the highest visitor taxes in Europe, according to the Barcelona City Council. That raised the total overnight tax for hotel guests to between $7.84 (€7.00) and $13.44 (€12.00) per person, per night, according to the Catalan Tax Agency. In September 2026, Barcelona also finalized plans to restrict short-stay cruise tourism. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The Barcelona City Council initially approved raising the municipal tourist tax surcharge for short-stay cruise visitors to the legal maximum of $27 per day, according to the official city council portal. Lippe-McGraw said the crowds are palpable in tourist areas, but the neighborhood where she lives is largely shielded from protests. "How do you decide who is allowed to come and see Venice or see Barcelona versus who is not?" "We were aware of this sort of anti-tourist sentiment before arriving, which definitely weighed on our minds," she said. "Some of Barcelona's most popular areas — like the Gothic Quarter, Las Ramblas, the Sagrada Familia — can be incredibly crowded even on a random Tuesday afternoon. "I can understand how frustrating that must be if you're a resident who's simply trying to get to work, running errands or going about your day." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Lippe-McGraw has traveled across all seven continents and said mass tourism has hit many major cities in her experience. "How do you decide who is allowed to come and see Venice or see Barcelona versus who is not?" she asked. Yet locals have been very welcoming to her family, she said. "Everybody has been welcoming us, even in day-to-day interactions at the store, at the pharmacy, dealing with a plumber," she said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "We are trying to make an effort to speak Spanish, learn the cultural norms. … And I think making an effort to understand the culture, learn the language and being respectful of local customs goes a long way." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Brittany Miller and Ashley J. DiMella of Fox News Digital, as well as Teresa Mull, contributed reporting.

articles.title: DOJ unveils nationwide tax fraud crackdown involving 76 defendants, nearly $500M in alleged losses
articles.summary: The Justice Department's first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge targeted 76 defendants across 35 U.S. attorneys' offices in a six-week crackdown.
articles.body: The Justice Department announced a nationwide tax fraud crackdown Wednesday involving 76 defendants and more than $490 million in estimated intended tax losses, including new charges against 31 individuals accused of schemes targeting American taxpayers. The first-ever National Tax Enforcement Surge brought together 35 U.S. attorneys' offices and IRS criminal investigators over approximately six weeks. The operation resulted in 23 new charging actions involving more than $350 million in alleged intended tax losses, while another 45 defendants were involved in trials, guilty pleas and sentencings associated with nearly $140 million in estimated intended losses. "Every dollar stolen through tax fraud is a dollar taken from the American people," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a news release "What we uncovered during this concentrated surge is only the tip of the iceberg. The Department of Justice is committed to expanding our investigations and exposing schemes designed to evade accountability, because there is no safe haven for fraudsters." AG BLANCHE UNVEILS FEDERAL CHARGES AGAINST 160 DEFENDANTS IN PANDEMIC RELIEF SWEEP Speaking at Wednesday's news conference, IRS Criminal Investigation chief Jarod Koopman described the operation as a new enforcement strategy and said similar crackdowns would follow. "The consolidated actions we are announcing today represent an entirely new approach in our enforcement strategy. Partnering with DOJ to strategically surge resources around a broad range of tax crimes. And although this type of enforcement is the first of its kind, it will not be the last," Koopman said. APPEALS COURT UPHOLDS ORDER BLOCKING IRS FROM SHARING TAXPAYER DATA WITH ICE Among the largest cases highlighted was an alleged fraudulent trust scheme in Texas, where four defendants were charged with promoting tax shelters that prosecutors say concealed more than $1.5 billion in income and caused over $200 million in estimated tax losses. In Georgia, three Mexican citizens were indicted in connection with an alleged $74 million tax refund scheme involving more than 16,000 U.S. Treasury checks. Prosecutors allege the defendants used Mexican identification documents belonging to other individuals to obtain IRS taxpayer identification numbers and file fraudulent returns. FBI OPERATION TARGETS SCAM COMPOUNDS IN AFRICA WITH ARRESTS, ACCOUNT TAKEDOWNS Asked during the news conference how much money taxpayers could expect to recover, Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald acknowledged that fraudulent proceeds are sometimes spent before investigators can retrieve them. McDonald said the Justice Department is building an asset forfeiture and recovery team to pursue assets allegedly purchased with fraud proceeds, including luxury vehicles and real estate. He did not provide a total recovery figure, noting that some cases remain in their early stages. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The crackdown follows the Justice Department's establishment of its National Fraud Enforcement Division in April. Defendants facing criminal charges are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

articles.title: The 41+ most exciting Advent calendars of the year: Bonne Maman, Squishmallows, Papier, Lego and more
articles.summary: Popular Advent calendars sell out before December, so get yours now. Shop the best ones from Bonne Maman, Anthropologie, Squishmallows and more.
articles.body: Traditionally, Advent calendars count down the days until Christmas. Some classic options have chocolate, caramels or other sweet treats hidden behind little doors, while others require you to turn on a light or check off a box leading up to the holiday. In recent years, however, Advent calendars have taken on a new life. Now, there’s an option for any holiday you celebrate, and they’re filled with coffee, wine, Legos, beauty products, pet treats and more. Because Advent calendars are so popular around the holidays, I recommend purchasing those you have your eye on as early as possible — they tend to sell out as we get closer to Christmas and Hanukkah. Below, I rounded up the best Advent calendars of 2026. You can buy them for yourself, but they’re great gifts for loved ones, too. I’ll frequently update this article throughout the next few weeks as more brands debut their Advent calendars (and sold-out options restock). Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Best Advent calendars overall I’m loyal to Bonne Maman jam, and every year, I look forward to its Advent calendar, which is filled with new limited-edition spreads. There’s a mini glass jar hidden inside each of the 24 boxes, and the festively decorated calendar opens like a book, which lets me stand it up on a shelf, doubling as holiday decor. This year, you’ll get to try spreads like caramel with salted butter, strawberry with Madagascar vanilla and raspberry with dark chocolate. Don’t worry if you can’t finish every jar before the end of the season — the spreads will last through June 2027, according to Bonne Maman. You can’t go wrong with a chocolate Advent calendar whether you’re buying it for yourself or gifting it to a loved one. It’s a classic for a reason, and getting to unwrap a new piece of chocolate every day is a small joy that anyone can appreciate. Lindt’s Advent calendar comes with 24 pieces of chocolate, including those shaped like mini bears, chocolate balls and chocolate neapolitans. For the first time this year, Lindt is adding an interactive element to its Advent calendar: From December 1 to 24, you can scan the QR code on the box to unlock the augmented reality experience, with new video drops daily. “The hot Advent calendar with the five-year-olds who can’t get the Needoh calendar is the Squishmallow calendar, so that’s what I’m buying for my daughter this year,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman. “As a mom, I appreciate that the smaller-sized stuffies will be easy to contain and don’t add a ton more clutter to our playroom, and my daughter will love seeing which cute character she gets each day.” This Advent calendar comes with 24 itty bitty Squishmallows stuffies that are 2.5 inches tall. Your recipient gets to collect popular characters like Junie the Banana, James the Fox, Cam the Cat and Benny the Bigfoot decked out in their holiday apparel. After opening this Advent calendar, you or your loved one will have an entire Lego Starwars scene to display or play with. There’s individual packs of Legos inside that come with a total of 293 blocks so you can build mini vehicles like an X-wing and The Razor Crest, as well as mini figurines like The Mandalorian, Grogu, the Blurrg, the Mudhorn and the Bantha. You also get a fold-out playmat to use as a backdrop. Lego says this Advent calendar is best for those ages 6 and up. Don’t wait to buy this beauty Advent calendar from Anthropologie — it’s usually one of the first to sell out because it’s so highly sought after. It’s filled with mini versions of the retailer’s bestselling products across skin care, makeup and fragrance, like Verb Ghost Oil, Salt & Stone deodorant, Caudalie eye cream and Peter Thomas Roth peptide cream. Anthropologie is also selling a 12 Days of Beauty Advent Calendar this year. Papier’s Advent calendar is as beautiful as it is useful. There’s 24 days worth of desk accessories inside, all of which are items you likely use every day at the office, home or school, like pens, journals, sticky tabs, highlighters, to-do notepads and stationary sets. Each item is individually wrapped in a paper box, which really makes it feel like you’re opening a gift every day. The Advent calendar, which folds open on the top and has three drawers, is designed to be a reusable organizer. Papier is also selling a 12-Day Advent Calendar for the first time this year. There are 12 Voluspa mini coconut wax candles inside this Advent calendar, each of which comes in a decorative glass votive. You’ll collect candles in a few of the brand’s bestselling scents, like white cypress, forbidden fig and santal vanille, as well as some holiday-specific fragrances like Gingerbread Chalet. The Advent calendar comes with a gold-plated wick trimmer, too. While I look forward to opening my own Advent calendar, I get even more excited about my dog’s. Last year was her first holiday season, so I started the tradition with her, which she’s thrilled about since it means extra snacks. If you want to do the same with a dog in your life, I recommend Himalayan Pet Supply’s calendar. It comes with 12 full-size yogurt sticks and churro chews in flavors like bacon, peanut butter, pumpkin, cheese and sweet potato. Best chocolate and candy Advent calendars Godiva’s Advent calendar has been one of our team’s favorites for years. It comes with 24 pieces of dark, milk and white chocolate, including dark chocolate caramels, milk chocolate creme puffs and birthday cake bliss white chocolates. There’s also a handful of star-shaped confections in there. Compartés’ popular Nutcracker and Winter Forest Advent calendars are back this year, plus the brand added a brand new one: the Enchanted Castle Advent calendar. There’s 24 chocolates inside, and each one has a different filling, like buttered croissant, espresso toffee, pistachio marzipan, cinnamon sugar donut and salted honeycomb. The calendar starts shipping on November 2. There’s plenty of candy-filled Advent calendars to choose from if you or your loved one don’t eat chocolate. Sugarfina’s is packed with the brand’s gummies, like sugared cranberries, sour rainbow bears, heavenly sours and magic mangos, plus there’s caramel and cereal balls. You get four pieces of candy per drawer for 24 days. Sugarfina is also selling a 12-day Advent calendar this year, as well as a Peanuts themed one. With this Advent calendar, you’ll get to snack on some of Dylan’s Candy Bar’s bestselling sweets leading up to the holidays, like cotton candy-flavored balls, blueberry candy sticks and fruit gummy stars. There are also seasonal candies inside, including green apple marshmallow Christmas trees, milk chocolate Santa’s helpers, gingerbread man lollipops and fruity gummy snowflakes. Best beauty Advent calendars L’Occitane’s Advent calendar is filled with 24 of the brand’s bestselling skin, body, hand and hair care products, many of which come highly recommended by NBC Selected commerce editor Cory Fernandez. “I love just about everything from L’Occitane, and it’s not only because everything smells amazing,” he says. “The products are also effective — they don’t have a greasy residue and don’t dry my skin or hair. Also, the Advent calendar is great because everything is the perfect sample size.” This holiday season, you’ll get to unbox L’Occitane’s popular hand creams, shower oil, exfoliating shower gel, fragrance and more, some of which are scented with the brand’s signature almond fragrance. Try 24 Sephora-brand skin care, makeup and bath products, as well as beauty tools, leading up to the holidays with this Advent calendar. It comes with 13 full-size and five travel-size items, plus six accessories. Each product is individually wrapped in its own numbered box, including a makeup sponge, hair clips, blush, face masks, mascara and eye cream. This is the ideal Advent calendar for the person who never leaves home without lip balm and has one in every bag they own. There’s 12 Burt’s Bees lip balms inside in flavors like sugar cookie, cinnamon apple crisp, vanilla bean and peppermint bark, the latter of which is exclusive to Amazon. The lip balms are all made with beeswax and vitamin E to soften and hydrate skin for up to 24 hours, according to the brand. The Glow Recipe Advent calendar is filled with 12 skin care finds, including the brand’s popular watermelon glow products, like the niacinamide drops, BHA toner and moisturizers. It also comes with multiple toner pads, a cleanser, a lip treatment and other products to help brighten and hydrate the skin, which is key heading into the winter months. Some of Charlotte Tilbury’s most beloved makeup and skin care products are hidden inside this treasure chest-shaped Advent calendar’s drawers. You get 15 items in total, four of which are full-size, including the Matte Revolution Lipstick and Hollywood Beauty Light Wand Highlighter in Pillow Talk, the Unreal Blush Healthy Glow Stick and a Lip Cheat Contour Duo. For the first time this year, the brand added two accessories to the calendar: a gua sha tool and a velvet makeup bag. Expand your lineup of Laneige skin care beyond the popular Lip Sleeping Mask with the K-beauty brand’s Advent calendar, which is filled with 12 products in full and mini sizes. You get the lip mask, of course, as well as face masks to put on before bed, moisturizer, cleanser, serums and lip balms. Laneige says the products are formulated with ingredients like peptides, hyaluronic acid and ceramides to help hydrate, plump and nourish skin. Best hair care Advent calendars Kitsch’s 12-day Advent calendar helps you refresh your collection of hair care and styling products. You get full-size items, most notably the brand’s beloved silk pillowcase — I own about six of them and sleep on one every night to protect my curls. The Advent calendar also includes clips, scrunches, a bonnet, hair perfume and shampoo and conditioner bars. There’s also two dermaplaning products for your face: dermaplaners and oil. The glitzy, glamorous hair accessories in Conair’s Advent calendar are exactly what you need to dress up any look, especially during the holiday season. It comes with 24 products, including bobby and hair pins, ponytail holders, clawclips and a scrunchie with a bow on it. You also get salon clips to help with skin care and makeup application, and a 2-in-1 mini boar slick back brush and taming wand. “My favorite thing about Teleties’ calendar is that it comes with exclusive pieces you can’t get otherwise, so it’s a great gift for someone who feels particularly special,” says NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans. The 12-day calendar comes with more than $100 worth of hair accessories, like claw clips, flat clips and different types of hair ties, some of which are holiday themed with festive prints and colors. Best nail Advent calendars Olive & June’s Advent calendar will upgrade your at-home manicures with 11 exclusive and previously sold out full-size nail polishes in a rainbow of shades. It also comes with two types of top coats: Sparkle Fairy Top Coat, which has an iridescent effect to it, and Long-Lasting Top Coat, which has a glossy finish. If you prefer a gel mani but want to do it yourself without the UV or LED light, Dazzle Dry’s Advent calendar is calling your name. It comes with everything you need to prep, paint, finish and touch up your nails, and directions that tell you which order to use all the products in. You get two exclusive full-size nail polish shades, as well as two sparkly minis. The polish is quick-drying and lasts for up to two weeks, according to the brand. Best wine and spirits Advent calendars Each of VineBox’s Advent calendars comes with 3.4-ounce sampler bottles of wine from across the world, and you get an insert with tasting notes and food pairing recommendations, a limited-edition art print and access to sommelier-led virtual tasting videos. So you could essentially host your own wine tastings at home. Vinebox sells three Advent calendars: the 12 Nights Velvet Collection, which comes with eight reds and four whites; the 12 Nights Vine Collection, which comes with six reds, one rosé and five distinctive wines; and the 24 Nights of Wine, which comes with all the wines in the Velvet and Vine collections. The 12 canned wines in this Advent calendar come from small-batch female- and minority-led wineries, and they have 0 grams of sugar, according to the brand. The cans are each equivalent to about one-third of a bottle, giving you about two glasses to share with someone or enjoy yourself. You get a mix of red, white, rosé and sparkling wines, plus a guide that provides links with in-depth information about each type. The calendar ships November 6. In Good Taste releases numerous wine Advent calendars every year, and it just debuted a Wine Cocktail Advent Calendar for the first time. There’s 24 ready-to-drink wine-based cocktails inside, including an espresso martini, piňa colada, mimosa, mojito and cosmopolitan. You get a 6-ounce serving of each one, as well as daily videos that pair with drinks so you can learn about tasting notes, food pairing suggestions and tips for garnishing. Best coffee and tea Advent calendars Instead of drinking the same type of coffee every morning, mix it up around the holidays with this Advent calendar. It comes with 24 K-Cups from brands like Caribou Coffee, Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, The Original Donut Shop and Peets, which you can pop into any compatible single-serve machine. In addition to standard, flavored and seasonal coffee pods, you also get hot cocoa and latte pods. No coffee maker? No problem. Cometeer’s coffee concentrate pods come frozen, and to turn one into a cup of joe, you just melt it with hot water. You can also melt the coffee in its capsule by leaving it in the refrigerator or at room temperature, and pour it over iced water to make iced coffee, or over hot or cold milk to make a latte. Cometeer’s Advent calendar comes with 24 pods from a handful of roasters the brand works with, like Birch, Joe Coffee and Red Bay Coffee. There are rare blends, single-origin roasts and festive holiday varieties. You have to store the calendar in the freezer to keep the pods frozen throughout the month. There’s 24 2-ounce packets of single-origin beans behind the doors of this Advent calendar, each of which makes about 24 ounces of pour-over coffee. You’ll get to try a new type of coffee every day from December 1 to Christmas Eve, so each one tastes a little different and you can learn about your preferences. In addition to the beans, you’ll get a custom 500-piece puzzle, access to Onyx’s web game and daily brew guides that share information about the coffee you’re drinking, recipes and stories from the Onyx team. Pukka’s Advent calendar folds out vertically, letting you hang it up and easily remove one tea sachet each day. You get 24 sachets in total, and they’re filled with organic herbal tea in flavors like night time, after dinner, mint, ginger, peppermint and licorice, and turmeric, ginger and orange. Tea Forte is known for its pyramid-shaped tea sachets, which lets the tea leaves unfurl and steep properly, making your beverage more flavorful and aromatic, according to the brand. There’s 12 sachets in this Advent calendar, including varieties like harvest apple spice, English breakfast, Moroccan mint and chocolate fondue. Tea Forte also sells five other Advent calendars that come with different types of tea: Warming Joy (24 days), Warming Joy Herbal (24 days), Volaré (12 days), Demoiselle (12 days) and Mariposa (12 days). Best food Advent calendars There are 24 all-butter shortbread cookies inside Walker’s Advent calendar, which takes care of dessert (at least somewhat) prior to the holidays. They come in six different shapes and flavors, like shortbread fingers, rounds, hearts and stars, as well as chocolate chip and salted caramel square cookies. As far as I’m concerned, Fishwife is responsible for making tinned fish a cool ingredient to snack on and add to meals, not something you ignore at the grocery store. The brand launched its first Advent calendar this year, which is filled with multiple cans of tinned fish, like smoked salmon, sardines, tuna and mussels. There’s also a handful of other surprises, like fish-shaped moisturizers from a collaboration with Bag Balm and a mini jar of hot sauce. Fly By Jing majorly upgraded its Advent calendar this year. It’s filled with a more diverse assortment of spicy surprises, including the brand’s bestsellers, brand-new sauces and beloved spice blends that were discontinued. You also get a unique ornament. Fly By Jing is selling a 24 day advent calendar, too, but very limited quantities are available. Baking cookies around the holidays is a tradition for many, and Williams Sonoma’s Advent calendar comes with lots of the supplies you need to whip up and package a batch. There’s 24 items inside, including cookie and biscuit cutters, piping bags, stencils, decorating tips, gift bags and spatulas. Best Advent calendars for kids After kids open all the doors of Magna-Tiles’ Advent calendar, they’ll be able to use the pieces to build a train that runs along a built-in track and create characters ready to board. It comes with exclusive figures you can mix and match the pieces of, as well as 10 decorated square blocks and three decorated triangle blocks. The Miffy lover in your life will look forward to finding out what stickers they’ll get from this Advent calendar leading up to the holidays. It comes with 12 sticker sheets; the recipient can use them on notebooks, toys, their clothes and coloring book pages. If the child (or adult) in your life is obsessed with Marvel, they’ll love adding these mini Funko Pop figures to their collection. The Advent calendar comes with 24 figures dressed in their winter gear, including Iron Man, Spiderman and Captain American. The little scientist in your life will have 24 days of hands-on activities to do in December with this Advent calendar. It comes with 13 kits for mini experiments and 11 specimens to study, like fossils and gemstones. And on Christmas Eve, they’ll get an extra special surprise: a sparkly piece of fool’s gold. Best Advent calendars for pets If your dog could talk they might agree that the 24 treats packed inside Wufers’ Advent calendar are as tasty as they are beautifully decorated. They come in festive shapes and when you open the calendar, it starts playing “Jingle Bells.” Costco members and non-members can shop Bark’s exclusive Advent calendar, which is packed with 24 goodies for your dog. They’ll get 16 treats and eight plush toys, including those with squeakers, crinkle-textured fabric and strong hairs to prevent shredding. Consider this Advent calendar a fun way to keep your cat(s) distracted from playing with your real or artificial Christmas tree. It comes with 12 toys: seven plush toys, two ball toys, a catnip toy, silvervine sticks and a teaser toy. Make playtime more exciting for your cat during the holidays with Chewy’s Frisco Advent calendar, which gives them 12 new toys to swat, kick, scratch and chase. They’ll get plush toys stuffed with silvervine and catnip, springs, plastic balls with bells, crinkle balls, feather teasers and more. There’s also a version for small dogs, which includes squeaky plush toys and several balls for them to play with. How I picked the best Advent calendars of 2026 To recommend the best Advent calendars, I researched highly-rated options across major categories like chocolate and candy, coffee and tea, food, wine and beauty. Every option on my final list comes from a brand we’ve previously covered or have personally tried. Some of the calendars were also sent to us as courtesy samples from brands or ones we bought with our own money. To evaluate each one, I assessed its contents, price and packaging. Our list includes options that countdown the 12, 24 and 25 days before a holiday. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected, where I’ve been writing gift guides for more than six years. I’ve specifically covered Advent calendars for the past four years. For this article, I compiled a list of the best Advent calendars of 2026, including highly-rated options, NBC Selected reader favorites and ones our team tested. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Colombia opposition groups launch protest against de la Espriella’s cuts
articles.summary: Former President Gustavo Petro joined thousands of demonstrators in Bogota in march against austerity, Israel ties.
articles.body:
A coalition of opposition parties, trade unions, indigenous groups and social movements has protested in Colombia against a series of economic and security policies advanced under right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella.

Thousands marched in major cities including the capital Bogota on Wednesday, the first day of a nationwide campaign led by the country’s former left-wing President Gustavo Petro.

Under Petro, Colombia expanded access to public universities, increased the minimum wage and improved labour protections for workers.

Opposition groups say many of those reforms are now under threat, as de la Espriella’s government embraces cuts to government programmes.

Colombia’s Congress has until Tuesday to approve its 2027 fiscal year budget. But as part of the new administration’s austerity measures, allies of de la Espriella are advancing proposals to reduce government spending.

De la Espriella has also pledged to turn Colombia away from his predecessor’s left-wing leanings and towards more free-market policies aligned with those of United States President Donald Trump.

The government issued new rules for police ahead of the protests, handing expanded powers to law enforcement to more quickly deal with protesters who vandalise public property or disrupt access to essential services.

“The right to protest is respected, but there is no right to destroy, attack the security forces, assault others or sow chaos,” de la Espriella said in a social media statement announcing the decree.

He added that “violence, vandalism and blockades that trample on the rights of millions of citizens will not be tolerated”.

Indigenous communities and political groups in rural parts of the country sometimes block roads as part of their protests, with impediments to traffic sometimes lasting weeks.

But critics have pointed out that the protests this week have been largely peaceful.

Many chanted “It will fall”, a reference to the perceived failure of de la Espriella’s government.

A former defence lawyer and millionaire businessman, de la Espriella was a political newcomer when he ran for the presidency this year on a far-right ticket.

He was elected in a June runoff race by a narrow margin. He campaigned on a hardline platform to address crime, immigration and the economy, including proposals to expel millions of migrants from Colombia and shrink the size of the government.

De la Espriella also pledged to backtrack on reforms made under Petro, Colombia’s first left-wing president. He took office in August.

A former left-wing fighter-turned-politician, Petro took part in protests on Wednesday. He was not eligible for re-election in this year’s presidential race; Colombian law currently caps presidents at a single term.

He wrote on social media that the mobilisations were a wake-up call “two months into the start of a tyrannical and imposed government”.

Protesters also expressed concerns about cuts to labour protections and healthcare under the new administration.

“I feel like we have no guarantees and that the little we did obtain … we’re about to lose,” teacher Ester Guerra, 32, told the news outlet AFP in Bogota.

Some demonstrators also took issue with the new administration’s overtures towards Israel. Several carried Palestinian flags, in a sign of solidarity.

On Wednesday, de la Espriella’s government opened a Colombian embassy in Jerusalem , a controversial move as Israel and Palestine have both claimed parts of the city.

Petro had been a staunch supporter of Palestine and had cut relations with Israel over its genocidal war against Gaza. But de la Espriella has moved to restore the severed ties since taking office.

That struck protesters like Jimena Rodriguez, a 20-year-old student, as an effort to ignore accusations of Israeli abuses against Palestinians.

Several noted that de la Espriella’s actions towards Israel mirrored Trump’s, who moved the US embassy to Jerusalem during his first term in 2018.

President de la Espriella “just wants to hand the country over to the United States, to Israel,” Rodriguez said. “I feel dark times are coming.”

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Wednesday assured voters complaining of irregular deletion from the Delhi electoral roll during SIR that on Oct 28 it will take care of their predicament caused by being asked to fill Form 6, which required a declaration that they are seeking inclusion in the voter lists for the first time.When advocate Prashant Bhushan sought urgent hearing on a petition to this effect by RTI activist Anjali Bhardwaj, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, "We are thinking of passing an order that will take care of it (the anomaly)."Deleted voters can’t claim to be first-timers’The bench proposed listing of Bhardwaj’s application for hearing on Oct 30. Bhushan said that it needs to be heard earlier given that EC has set Oct 30 as the last date for correcting the discrepancy in the draft voter list. SC agreed to hear the application on Oct 28.Draft electoral roll of Delhi, published on Aug 31, noted that of the 1,45,10,299 voters who were on the rolls before SIR began, 97,53,577 have submitted enumeration forms, while 47,56,722 were excluded from the draft roll under absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) categories. EC had extended the time for filing claims and objections from Sep 30 to Oct 30.Bhardwaj said the only mechanism prescribed for the “irregularly” deleted voters to re-enter their names in electoral roll is by filling Form 6, which makes it mandatory for the applicant to make a declaration that he/she is seeking inclusion in the voter list for the first time, which will be factually incorrect.Of the 47.56 lakh excluded, nearly 32 lakh are categorised as permanently shifted. Bhushan suggested that EC could be directed to allow those seeking reentering of names in voter lists to apply using Form 8 or use another appropriate mechanism to restore/include names of existing electors that do not figure in the draft rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: John Cena granted 650 wishes for children with critical illnesses; the WWE star earned a Guinness World Records title in 2022
articles.summary: John Cena’s wrestling career has taken him from packed arenas to film sets, but a different part of his public life has involved meeting children living
articles.body: John Cena’s wrestling career has taken him from packed arenas to film sets, but a different part of his public life has involved meeting children living with critical illnesses. Since 2002, the American wrestler and actor has made time for requests handled by the Make-A-Wish Foundation, an organisation that arranges experiences for children facing serious medical conditions. Guinness World Records reported that by September 2022, his contribution had reached a record 650 wishes, earning him recognition from Guinness World Records. The figure placed Cena ahead of every other celebrity involved with the charity, following two decades in which he continued to accept requests alongside the demands of his career in professional wrestling and entertainment.The WWE ambassador has secured his place in pop culture and the record books as a Guinness World Records ICON. His induction will be featured in Guinness World Records 2027, as reported.John Cena’s Make-A-Wish journey began in 2002Cena’s association with Make-A-Wish started three years after he entered professional wrestling in 1999. At the time, his career was still developing, and his later success in WWE had yet to take shape. His first wish for the charity marked the beginning of a relationship that would eventually extend across hundreds of meetings with children and their families.Make-A-Wish works with children aged between two and 18 who have been diagnosed with critical illnesses. Their requests vary according to individual interests and circumstances. Some children want to meet a favourite public figure, while others ask to attend a particular event or receive a gift for themselves or someone else.For Cena, the requests became a recurring part of his life outside wrestling. The number of wishes he granted grew over the years, eventually putting him well ahead of other celebrities who had participated in the programme.Guinness World Records recognised John Cena for his charitable milestoneIn September 2022, Guinness World Records reported that Cena had granted 650 wishes through Make-A-Wish, establishing a record for the most wishes granted through the foundation. The milestone followed an earlier occasion when he was recognised for reaching 500.According to Guinness World Records, no other celebrity had granted more than 400 wishes during the organisation’s 42-year history at the time of its report. Cena was also described as the foundation’s most requested celebrity, reflecting the demand among children hoping to meet him.The record was not based on a single event or a short period of charitable activity. It represented a commitment that had developed over roughly 20 years, running alongside his work as a professional wrestler and, increasingly, as an actor.Why John Cena was willing to drop everything to grant a child’s wishCena has spoken about his willingness to respond when Make-A-Wish contacts him. He said: "If you ever need me for this ever, I don’t care what I’m doing, I will drop what I’m doing and be involved because I think that’s the coolest thing.""I just drop everything," Cena said when he was honoured for granting 500 wishes."If I can offer a fantastic experience, I’ll be first in line to do my part."Those remarks offered an explanation for how his total had continued to rise despite a demanding professional schedule. Wrestling appearances, filming and other commitments can leave limited room for additional engagements. Cena’s stated willingness to rearrange his plans gave the charity a measure of consistency in arranging meetings with him.John Cena gives children a chance to meet their wrestling heroFor children who choose Cena, the experience can involve more than a brief introduction. Meetings may include photographs, conversation and time spent with the wrestler. Some children have also had the chance to venture inside a wrestling ring, bringing them closer to the sport they follow.Cena often appears with one of his championship belts, a reminder of the career that made him recognisable to young fans. He has held the WWE Championship 13 separate times, won the World Heavyweight Championship three times and captured the United States Championship five times, according to the Guinness World Records report.John Cena’s journey from wrestling fame to granting 650 wishesCena entered WWE in 1999 and became one of its most prominent performers. A 16-time world champion, he built a public identity around his wrestling persona before moving into acting and other entertainment work. His involvement in WWE’s Be a Star anti-bullying campaign also extended his public-facing work beyond competition in the ring.Make-A-Wish became another part of that activity. Founded to fulfil wishes for children with critical illnesses, the charity offers experiences shaped by the interests of the children it serves. Meeting a celebrity is one option, alongside attending events and other personal requests.Cena is not the only well-known figure to have taken part. Justin Bieber, Lady Gaga, Selena Gomez and Samuel L. Jackson have also granted wishes through the foundation. By the time his total reached 650 in 2022, however, Cena had established a record that separated his contribution from those of other celebrity participants.You use AI every day.
